subQuestions.questionText:
Thabo, a soccer fan from Johannesburg, is flying to Mexico City for the 2026 FIFA World Cup (departure 22:00, total flight duration 18 hours including a 7-hour layover in London).

Determine the number of time zones Thabo will cross when flying from Johannesburg to Mexico City.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: 8 time zones (2 marks)
Johannesburg is +2 and Mexico City is -6, so Thabo crosses 8 time zones.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the term long-haul flight.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks): A flight that covers a long distance with a duration of 6 hours or longer (a flight of more than 6 hours).
NOTE: Learners must mention the number of hours.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Thabo's arrival time in Mexico City.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mexico City: -6; Johannesburg: +2
Time difference = 8 hours
Local time in Mexico = 22:00 - 8 hours = 14:00
Flying time = 18 hours
Arrival time in Mexico = 14:00 + 18 hours = 08:00

Final answer: 08:00
[Award full 5 marks for the correct final answer with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText:
The opening ceremony in Mexico City will be at 20:00 local time.

Determine the time in Johannesburg when South Africans will be able to view the ceremony live on television.
subQuestions.memoText:
Local time in Mexico City = 20:00
Time difference = 8 hours
Time in Johannesburg = 20:00 + 8 hours = 04:00

Final answer: 04:00
[Award full 4 marks for the correct final answer.]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO important travel documents that Thabo will require to enter Mexico.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (1 mark each):
• Valid passport
• Valid visa

Thabo arrived in Mexico City and was completely exhausted.

Name the condition that Thabo suffered from after having crossed many time zones.

subQuestions.memoText:

• Disorientation

subQuestions.questionText:
Before his trip, Thabo visited a travel clinic for advice on recommended and compulsory vaccinations required to enter Mexico.

Explain ONE difference between recommended and compulsory vaccinations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks each):
Recommended vaccination: a vaccine that is advised for travellers based on their destination and is NOT legally required for entry.
Compulsory vaccination: a vaccine that is legally required for entry into certain countries to prevent the spread of certain diseases.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why Thabo should avoid drinking tap water in Mexico.
subQuestions.memoText:

• Drinking tap water in Mexico may make Thabo susceptible (vulnerable) to waterborne diseases.

subQuestions.label: 2.3.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ONE way in which Thabo can ensure his safety when using a taxi service.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Use only registered or app-based taxi services.
• Avoid unmarked taxis as they may be unsafe.
• Use e-hailing services that can be tracked on a fully charged smartphone.
• Check vehicle identification and/or driver ratings before using the service.
• Be vigilant and do not display valuables while waiting on or in the taxi.

subQuestions.label: 2.3.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ONE way in which Thabo can ensure his safety by learning a few Spanish phrases.
subQuestions.memoText:

Knowing basic Spanish phrases could help Thabo communicate quickly and clearly with locals or authorities when an unsafe situation/emergency arises.

subQuestions.questionText:
A tourist travelling to London exchanges South African rand for Great British pound at Cape Town International Airport before departing South Africa.

Exchange rate table:
| Currency | BBR | BSR |
| Euro | 18,76 | 19,79 |
| Great British pound | 22,50 | 23,50 |
| US dollar | 17,29 | 18,15 |

Give the currency code for the Great British pound.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer: GBP (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the following term: Fluctuation of exchange rates.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
Fluctuation refers to the continuous rise and fall in the exchange rate / the changing value of one currency when compared to another.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the following term: Bank buying rate.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
The bank buying rate is the rate at which the bank buys foreign currency.

subQuestions.questionText: Using the exchange rate table (GBP: BBR 22,50 / BSR 23,50), calculate how many Great British pounds a tourist would receive if he exchanged ZAR20 000. (Round off to TWO decimal places.) (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
R20 000 ÷ 23,50 (Bank Selling Rate — the bank sells GBP to the tourist)
= GBP851,06

Final answer: £851,06 (851,06 Great British pound / pound sterling)
[Award full 3 marks for the correct final answer with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText: Using the exchange rate table (GBP: BBR 22,50 / BSR 23,50), calculate how many rands a tourist will receive when exchanging 200 Great British pounds on arrival in South Africa. (Round off to TWO decimal places.) (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
GBP200 × 22,50 (Bank Buying Rate — the bank buys GBP from the tourist)
= R4 500,00

Final answer: R4 500,00 (ZAR4 500,00)
[Award full 3 marks for the correct final answer with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why a tourist should consider the exchange rates offered by the different forex kiosks at the airport, before exchanging money.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
The tourist needs to carefully manage his foreign exchange transactions to avoid high fees and unfavourable exchange rates.
• Considering different rates ensures the best value for his currency.

• It is a sacred mountain to the local communities.

subQuestions.label: 4.1.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways, except for litter control, in which sustainable and responsible management practices can be implemented at this mountain (Mount Everest). (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)

• Promote awareness and education of responsible practices when climbing the mountain.

subQuestions.label: 4.1.4(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why it is important to have sustainable and responsible practices at the mountain (Mount Everest). (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• It helps to reduce pollution on the climbing trails.
• It helps with the protection of the natural environment.
• It protects the climbers, as too many people on the mountain can be a risk factor.
• It protects the culture of the local communities.
• It prevents animals from dying after ingesting litter.
• It helps to curb global warming and the melting of glaciers.

The Maya train was named after the ancient Mayan civilization (tribe/indigenous people) from Chichen Itza.

• It creates greater awareness, attracting many tourists and leading to positive spin-offs for the icon.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which the Maya train can add to the success of Chichen Itza as an attraction. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• The Maya train brings more tourists to the area, which brings more income for the area.
• The train links Chichen Itza to other popular tourist attractions.
• The Maya train makes Chichen Itza more accessible and convenient for tourists.

questions.title: Culture and Heritage Tourism — The Nelson Mandela Legacy Sites

Explain how TOMSA gets funding for local and international marketing of South Africa.

• He is wearing excessive jewellery.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain what the manager means by dress to impress.
subQuestions.memoText:

• Dress appropriately for the position that you are employed for.
• Dress in a way that makes customers feel confident about what your business has to offer.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which it will be to the advantage of the business if all staff members adhere to the dress code.

Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Creates a professional and trustworthy image of the company.
• Helps customers easily identify staff members.
• Promotes teamwork and a sense of belonging.
• Sets a standard for an acceptable level of hygiene and cleanliness.
• Ensures safety by wearing the right attire for the job.
• Makes the company look well-organised and consistent, which may lead to positive word of mouth.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE way in which a manager can guide an employee who does not adhere to the dress code of the business.

• Explain to the employee the importance of adhering to the dress code of the company.
• Provide support, such as suggesting where to get the correct uniform.
• Take further action if the employee continues to ignore the rules.

• Providing excellent customer service.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why airlines must have clear conditions of employment for cabin crew members.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• To ensure there is efficiency in the airline's daily operations.
• To ensure that cabin crew embrace professionalism.
• To ensure safety on board.
• To ensure fair treatment and job security for the cabin crew.
• It protects the employer and the employee.

subQuestions.questionText:
When tourists go on a hiking tour, it is important for them to act responsibly (for example by disposing of litter in the bins provided).

Being a responsible tourist means respecting the natural environment by following the rules and considering the impact of their actions on the environment.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of disposing of litter into the bins provided.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• It helps to keep hiking paths and the environment beautiful and safe for other hikers.
• It protects wildlife that may swallow the litter.
• It protects natural resources, keeps the environment clean and fosters respect for the environment.
• It can assist in recycling efforts.
• It can reduce pollution.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO alternatives (something else) to carry water while hiking instead of using single-use plastic water bottles.

• Make use of water stations provided by some parks, reducing the need for single-use plastic bottles.
NOTE: Accept examples of refillable, environmentally friendly alternatives to carry water.

subQuestions.questionText:
The removal of alien and invasive plants in nature reserves is an important step in promoting environmental sustainability.

State ONE negative impact on nature if alien plants are left to grow wild and uncontrolled.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Alien plants can harm local ecosystems by competing with indigenous species and disrupting the balance of nature.
• They are usually water-hungry plants and might put a strain on water resources.
• Some invasive alien plants increase the risk of veld fires.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE benefit for the Kloofendal Nature Reserve when members/supporters of the community project remove invasive plants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Supporters of the community project help preserve the natural biodiversity of the area.
• Removing alien invasive plants supports healthy ecosystems.
• Indigenous plant species will flourish.
• Restoring the biodiversity can be done in a shorter period of time.
• Promotes positive publicity, attracting more visitors.

subQuestions.questionText:
A massive fire at an electrical substation near London Heathrow International Airport (United Kingdom) on 21 March 2025 forced Heathrow to shut down operations for 18 to 28 hours. Over 1 300 flights were delayed, cancelled or diverted, affecting around 300 000 passengers.

Name the continent where this global event happened.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer (2 marks): Europe

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO disruptions to airline operations caused by the fire outbreak.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Delays in flights
• Cancelled flights
• Diverted flights
• Grounding of flights
• Inconvenienced passengers
• Stranded passengers
• Disrupted electricity supply

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO economic impacts that this event had on the global tourism industry.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Airports and airlines incurred extra costs to reroute planes.
• Stranded passengers needed accommodation.
• Passengers would have been compensated for the delays.
• Travel-dependent businesses (hotels, car rentals, tour operators) suffered from lost bookings.
• Travellers cancelled or rescheduled trips, impacting destinations that rely on international visitors.
• Travel-dependent businesses in areas where flights were rerouted benefitted from the disruption.
NOTE: Answers must refer to the economic impact on global tourism-dependent businesses, not the economy of the UK.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE advantage the 23% increase in geographical spread will have for the tourism industry in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• The lesser-visited provinces will gain economically from the increase in geographical spread.
• Increase of visitor numbers to the less-visited provinces.
• More provinces will stand to gain better returns on their marketing efforts.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO reasons why African land markets contribute the largest percentage of tourist arrivals in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Favourable visa requirements allow for easier access into South Africa.
• Tourists enter South Africa primarily for shopping opportunities and to visit friends and relatives.
• Availability of various affordable transport options and shorter land routes, making South Africa more accessible.

questions.title: Communication and Customer Care — Customer Feedback

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why a customer's feedback can be considered to be a gift to the business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
The business will be able to maintain or improve their services in order to retain and increase their customer base.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE way in which the business can change an unhappy customer to a happy customer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Listen attentively to make the customer feel heard and valued.
• Apologise for the poor service.
• Offer an immediate solution.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO methods, other than real-time feedback and handwritten surveys, a business can use to collect customer feedback.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Online surveys that capture customer responses.
• Employing people to gather feedback through one-on-one interviews with customers.
• Follow-up phone calls.
• Web-based responses.
• SMS and e-mails to gather feedback.

subQuestions.questionText:
Real-time feedback is when suggestions or criticism is shared during and after a service is provided.

Explain ONE way in which this will benefit a business more than a handwritten survey.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Real-time feedback allows for immediate action and responses to the issue at hand, while handwritten surveys may delay the process.
• Real-time feedback is more accurate, as the responses are provided when the experience is still fresh.
• The response rate is faster with real-time feedback, leading to better customer care.
• Real-time feedback is more personal than handwritten survey responses.
